name: Sheep Creek Campground
note: WA DNR forest campground on Big Sheep Creek Rd north of Northport (Colville-area trust land); nearly closed but saved by the Town of Northport and now DNR-maintained with Discover Pass funds. Small forested campground (~11 sites) along both banks of Sheep Creek, hand water pump, 1 ADA site. Sites accommodate up to a 24-ft trailer with a tight tree-lined turnaround - fits a 23-ft rig but not larger ones. First-come, first-served (Discover Pass required). --Claude

name: Home Valley Park & Campground
note: Skamania County park in the Columbia River Gorge at Home Valley. 23 first-come, first-served campsites, no hookups; suitable for tents, truck campers and RVs (satellite shows full-size trailers, so a 23-ft rig fits). Ballfields, river/gorge access; adjacent BNSF rail line brings train noise. --Claude

name: Grays Harbor County Fair Campground
note: Grays Harbor County Fair & Event Center in Elma. Year-round first-come, first-served campground: over a hundred water/electric sites plus some full-hookup sites and dry/tent camping across the grounds; showers/restrooms. Off-peak and peak nightly rates (with/without hookup). --Claude

name: Palouse Empire Fairgrounds
note: Whitman County fairgrounds 5 mi west of Colfax; the county permits camping year-round, not just during the fair. Grassed sites with water + electric, RVs to 50 ft, dump station, restrooms/showers plus pit toilets; RV self-serve check-in, no reservations (first-come, first-served). County-operated (pef@co.whitman.wa.us). --Claude

name: Salt Creek Recreation Area
note: Clallam County park on a bluff above the Strait of Juan de Fuca near Joyce; 92 campsites (some utility/electric sites), ~73 with a water view. Reservable Feb 1-Oct 31 via CampLife plus FCFS kiosks. --Claude

name: Dungeness Recreation Area Campground
note: Clallam County park on the bluff above the Strait of Juan de Fuca, ~7 mi NW of Sequim adjoining Dungeness Spit NWR; 66 forested sites in two loops, no hookups (33 reservable, 31 FCFS, 2 host). Reservable Feb 1-Oct 31 plus FCFS kiosks. --Claude

name: Wenberg County Park
note: Snohomish County park on the east shore of Lake Goodwin; 70 sites in three loops (full, partial water/power, and non-utility), enclosed swim beach and two-lane boat launch. Reservable online with drop-in/FCFS for unreserved sites. --Claude

name: Quilcene Campground
note: Jefferson County Parks & Rec campground on US 101 in Quilcene, next to the community center. 9 wooded sites (picnic table + fire ring), toilet, fresh water; RVs to ~30 ft. First-come, first-served, open ~Apr 1-Oct 31. --Claude

name: Coulee City Community Park
note: Town of Coulee City municipal campground on Banks Lake; full-hookup + dry/tent sites (aggregators cite ~55 full-hookup / 100+ total), showers, laundry, dump station, boat launch & marina, adjacent day-use park. First-come, first-served (self-pay kiosk, no reservations); open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Liberty Lake Regional Park Campground
note: Spokane County's Liberty Lake Regional Park campground; 17 standard RV sites (water+electric) + 3 full-hookup premium + tent sites, showers, central dump station, set in forest at the park's south end (Liberty Lake ~1 km north, separate swim area). Reservable online + FCFS for unreserved; open ~mid-May to late Sept. --Claude

name: Grandy Lake Park
note: Skagit County park on Grandy Lake off Baker Lake Rd near Concrete; ~20 primitive drive-in dirt/gravel sites (best for tents and small-to-mid RVs), fire rings, flush toilet, dump station. Self-pay $15/night, first-come first-served, 14-day max; winter (Nov 1-Feb 28) self-contained units only. --Claude

name: Sauk Park
note: 40-acre Skagit County park on the Sauk River, ~12.8 mi north of Darrington on Concrete-Sauk Valley Rd. Spacious treed drive-in sites (most with picnic table & fire pit), trail down to the river, laundry. First-come, first-served, $15/night (self-pay); open Mar 1-Oct 31, self-contained units only Nov-Feb. --Claude

name: Okanogan County Fairgrounds RV Park
note: Okanogan County fairgrounds RV park at 175 Rodeo Trail Rd, operating as a public RV campground (open year-round except the county-fair closure, ~late Aug-mid Sep). 64 full-hookup sites, 44 electric/water sites, plus dry/tent camping; showers, restrooms, Wi-Fi. Reservable online (Firefly), FCFS otherwise. --Claude

name: Chewelah City Park
note: City of Chewelah-operated municipal park off US-395 with Chewelah Creek running through it. ~10-14 RV sites with 30-amp power + water hookups plus a couple tent sites; RVs to ~35 ft on gravel pads. First-come, first-served, honor-system payment (envelope at entrance, ~$10-20/night), short max stay (~3-5 days). Playground, restrooms, shade trees, amphitheater. --Claude

name: Swauk Campground
note: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Cle Elum RD) campground in a ponderosa pine/larch grove along Swauk Creek near Blewett Pass, ~26 mi NE of Cle Elum on Hwy 97/970; 19 single + 2 double nonelectric sites, no hookups/water/dump, narrow interior road best for rigs under ~30 ft. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay on-site). --Claude

name: Washington Park Campground
note: City of Anacortes Parks & Rec campground in 220-acre Washington Park on Fidalgo Island (Rosario Strait), by the San Juan ferry terminal; 68 sites - 46 with water/electric, 22 no-hookup - plus 25 first-come, first-served sites, showers, dump station, open year-round. Reservable online with FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Kulshan Campground
note: Large campground on the west shore of Baker Lake maintained by Puget Sound Energy (utility operator), ~8 mi north of Concrete just south of Baker Dam off SR 20; ~108 tent/RV drive-in sites, main loop has water and sewer hookups, overflow loop is dry camping; first-come, first-served (free dry camping off-season). Boat launches nearby. --Claude

name: Boundary Dam Campground
note: Campground operated by Seattle City Light (city municipal utility) at Boundary Dam/Reservoir on the Pend Oreille River, NE corner of WA. 22 sites (3 ADA), roughly 12 that fit RVs (Class C-size), no hookups; flush toilets, potable water, trash, boat launch and dock, day-use area. First-come, first-served, 6-day max stay. --Claude

name: Alfred A. Loeb State Park
note: Oregon State Parks campground in an old-growth myrtlewood grove on the Chetco River ~8 mi inland (NE) of Brookings. ~53 sites with 50-amp electrical and water (no full hookups, no dump station), plus 3 reservable log cabins; flush toilets and hot showers. Campsites are first-come, first-served (cabins reservable online). --Claude

name: Jubilee Lake Campground
note: Jubilee Lake Campground, Umatilla National Forest (federal, not state despite the RV Life tag) on Jubilee Lake — 48 tent/RV sites + 5 tent-only, high-elevation spruce-fir setting; pull-through and some back-in sites fit longer rigs. Boat ramp (non-motorized/electric-troll only). Mostly reservable on recreation.gov, some FCFS. --Claude

name: Cascara Campground (Fall Creek State Recreation Area)
note: Cascara Campground at Fall Creek State Recreation Area on Fall Creek Reservoir (RV Life mis-spells it 'Casara') — 39 drive-in primitive sites (potable water, vault toilets) among Douglas firs; boat launch and swim area, amphitheater; some sites with lake views. Open ~May 1–Sep 30. First-come, first-served (the adjacent Fisherman's Point group camp is reservable). --Claude

name: Red Bridge State Wayside
note: Oregon State Parks wayside on the Grande Ronde River along OR-244 southwest of La Grande, in ponderosa pine/cottonwood. ~10 back-in RV sites plus ~10 tent sites, primitive (no hookups) with running water and flush toilets. First-come, first-served, open ~May 1-Oct 14. --Claude

name: McCubbins Gulch Campground
note: Mt. Hood National Forest (USFS, Barlow RD) rustic campground about 25 miles west of Maupin off County Rd 216 / FR 2110. ~15 first-come, first-served sites (no hookups), vault toilet, many sites adjacent to McCubbins Creek; vehicles 25 ft max. Within the McCubbins Gulch OHV trail area (expect OHV noise); seasonal, roughly May-Sept. --Claude

name: Nehalem Falls Campground
note: Oregon Dept. of Forestry campground in the Tillamook State Forest along the Nehalem River, about 13 miles east of Manzanita on Foss Road. 14 drive-in sites (no hookups) plus 6 walk-in tent sites and 1 reservable group site; vault toilets, hand-pump water, camp host. Drive-in sites are first-come, first-served (max length listed to 40 ft, but small forest loop — best for rigs up to the mid-20s). --Claude

name: River Bridge Campground
note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (High Cascades RD) on the Upper Rogue River off FR 6210 near Prospect; 9 single sites + 2 OHV sites, RVs/trailers OK, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (cashless Scan-and-Pay as of 7/2026); open ~May-Nov. --Claude

name: Island Campground
note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Powers RD). Small primitive 5-site campground in a myrtlewood grove on the South Fork Coquille River, ~17 mi south of Powers on FR3300; vault toilet, no drinking water, no hookups; gravel drive-in access (any vehicle) with a small parking area, best for smaller rigs. First-come, first-served, fee. --Claude

name: Oak Flat Campground
note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Gold Beach RD). ~15 sites on a flat above the Wild & Scenic Illinois River near Agness (Illinois River West trailhead); vault toilet, no water, no hookups; agency lists it as small-trailers-only with a rough gravel access road (CR450) - best for smaller rigs. First-come, first-served, fee. --Claude

name: Daley Creek Campground
note: Small USFS campground (Rogue River-Siskiyou NF, High Cascades RD) near the confluence of Beaver Dam and Daley Creeks off Dead Indian Memorial Hwy / FR 37. 6 sites (3 tent, 3 designated trailer sites), vault toilet, no potable water, pack-out trash; drive-in on maintained gravel forest road. First-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct. --Claude

name: Mount Ashland Campground
note: Rustic USFS campground (Klamath NF, on the Siskiyou crest in Oregon) 1 mi south of Mt. Ashland Ski Resort, ~10.5 mi up FR 20 from I-5. 9 sites accommodating small RVs/trailers to ~28 ft, no potable water, pack-out trash. First-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct once FR 20 clears of snow; elev ~6,600 ft. --Claude

name: Cabin Lake Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) FCFS camping area at the historic 1920s-30s Fort Rock Ranger Station site in open ponderosa/grassland, reached via graveled Cabin Lake Rd (FS 18). Rustic, open sites accommodate RVs to ~30 ft; no potable water, vault toilet, open year-round. Known for bird-viewing blinds. --Claude

name: Pine Mountain Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) campground on the summit of Pine Mountain by Pine Mountain Observatory, ~34 mi SE of Bend. 6 primitive sites, First-come, first-served. Vault toilets, no potable water. Gravel access road; small trailers fine, larger rigs need a careful driver on tight turns. --Claude

name: Soda Creek Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) campground beside Soda Creek where it flows through an open meadow into Sparks Lake, Cascade Lakes Hwy. 10 sites, no hookups; limited RV-friendly sites, max spur 40 ft. Vault toilets, no potable water (bring your own). Reservable, FCFS if unbooked. --Claude

name: Big Elk Campground
note: Siuslaw NF (Central Coast RD) campground on Big Elk Creek near Blodgett, ~10 mi off US-20; last ~3 mi washboard gravel, passable by any vehicle. ~10-12 primitive drive-in sites plus a hiker/biker site, First-come, first-served; no hookups, no potable water, pit toilets. Concession-managed. --Claude

name: French Pete Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (McKenzie River RD) campground at the confluence of French Pete Creek and the South Fork McKenzie River, ~1,800 ft, on Forest Rd 19. 17 shaded sites (CCC-era developed campground) with vault toilets, hand-pump water, fire rings; mix of FCFS and reservable. --Claude

name: McKenzie Bridge Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (McKenzie River RD) campground in a grove of Douglas fir and western red cedar along the McKenzie River, ~1 hr E of Eugene off Hwy 126. 20 sites (max trailer 35 ft), vault toilets, drinking water, on-site boat ramp; mix of FCFS and reservable. FS notes all sites have river access. --Claude

name: Gerber Reservoir Recreation Area
note: BLM (Klamath Falls Field Office), on Gerber Reservoir ~42 mi east of Klamath Falls. North and South Campgrounds total ~50 primitive sites (no hookups) with drinking water, vault toilets, RV dump station, and gravel/concrete boat ramps; drive-in, first-come first-served. A separate 7-site horse camp is also present. Fees collected in peak season (May-Sep). --Claude

name: Ludlum Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Gold Beach Ranger District), adjacent to the Winchuck River and Wheeler Creek near the CA line SE of Brookings. 7 sites, all accommodate tents/trailers/RVs to 32 ft; drinking water, vault toilets; first-come first-served (the separate Ludlum House is a group cabin rental on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Nook Bar
note: Dispersed camping on an open gravel bar along the Wild and Scenic Chetco River, ~3 mi up FR 1376 (North Bank Chetco River Rd) from the forest boundary in Rogue River-Siskiyou NF. Wide open gravel bar fits larger rigs; primitive, no hookups or water. Cashless Scan & Pay via recreation.gov, FCFS. Winter gravel-bar camping discouraged due to frequent high-water events. --Claude

name: Fourbit Ford Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest (High Cascades RD) campground on Fourbit Creek about a mile off Butte Falls-Prospect Hwy. 7 sites, vault toilet, no potable water (water available at nearby Whiskey Springs), no hookups. Narrow access road not recommended for rigs over ~30 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits. Primarily first-come, first-served (rec.gov scan-and-pay from 7/2026). --Claude

name: Whiskey Springs Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest campground near Butte Falls, a short distance from Willow Lake. 34 sites (7 tent-only, rest fit RVs/trailers, 5 pull-throughs), water faucets and flush/vault toilets, no hookups; a 1-mile interpretive loop trail runs through it. Trailers over 28 ft not recommended, so a 23-ft rig fits. Reservable on recreation.gov plus some FCFS. --Claude
